en: Itivuttaka 82:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on the Sounds of Gods.
This was said by the Blessed One; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three sounds of the gods that issue forth among the gods from time to time."
Which three?

Bhikkhus, at whatever time a noble disciple, having shaved off his hair and beard and donned saffron robes, intends to go forth from the household life into homelessness—at that time a cry of "deva" goes out among the devas:
"This noble disciple intends to do battle with Māra."
“Monks, this is the first divine sound that issues forth among the gods from time to time.
Furthermore, monks, on whatever occasion a noble disciple dwells devoted to the practice of developing the seven factors of enlightenment, on that occasion a divine sound issues forth among the gods:
‘This noble disciple is engaged in battle with Māra.’”
This, monks, is the second divine sound that resounds among the gods from time to time.
Furthermore, monks, on whatever occasion a noble disciple, through the destruction of the taints,
dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it...
At such a time, among the gods, a divine cry goes forth:
‘This noble disciple has conquered the battle; having completely triumphed at the head of that very battle, he dwells there.
This, monks, is the third divine cry that goes forth among the gods from time to time.
“Monks, these three divine sounds arise among the gods from time to time.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. With reference to this, it is said:
“Having seen one who has conquered the battle,
a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
even the deities pay him homage.”
Great and free from timidity.
Homage to you, O noble steed among men,
who have overcome that which is difficult to conquer!
Having conquered the army of Death,
through unobstructed liberation—
thus indeed do they pay homage to him.
The deities see his mind;
for they do not see that by which he would fall under the power of death.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The third [sutta].
